h: The field which the Lord has blessed

p: — The field of Machpelah is called
— "a field which the Lord has blessed,"
, — as is written in the holy Zohar.
— And after the Binding of Isaac,
— when Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, was made complete
— "And Avraham was old, come into the days"
, — as is written in the holy Zohar
— then he bought the field of Machpelah
— And it is brought in the holy Zohar (127a)
, — the entrance of the Garden of Eden there.
— that supernal fragrances would rise up,
, — coming out from within the cave, etc.
— And this is the fragrance of
— "a field which the Lord has blessed":
— the fragrance of the Garden of Eden.
— in the passage of "Let there be light"
— correspond to the five books of the Torah,
, — as is written in Bereishis Rabbah;
— that is, the light of Torah
— which are the two letters hei.
— in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar:
, — the Ten Utterances of the Torah."
,, — as is written in the holy Zohar.

p: — what have the sons of Heth
— to do with the Ten Commandments,
— that they should be mentioned ten times

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 58:8 — "How much ink is poured out … to write 'the sons of Heth'! Ten times 'the sons of Heth' is written … corresponding to the Ten Commandments, to teach that whoever clarifies a tzaddik's purchase is as if he fulfilled the Ten Commandments." This midrash sets the question the whole maamar answers. It is also brought in Yalkut Shimoni, Chayei Sarah §102 ("How much ink is poured out").

h: "Your father the Amorite, your mother a Hittite"

p: עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד עַמּוּד ב)
שֶׁכְּשֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִיחֶזְקֵאל
— that when the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Yechezkel,
— and your mother a Hittite,' etc.,"
— surely Terach was of the sons of Shem,
— as stated explicitly in the Torah,
— and from them came Avraham and Sarah!
— according to what our master wrote,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
— may the memory of the holy tzaddik be for a blessing for the life of the World to Come,
— corresponds to the middah of Gevurah —
— from the word chittas, dread and fear —
— it is the trait of jealousy;
— with regard to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
— who drew the holiness and the vitality out of them.
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג קפד עַמּוּד א)
— and was of the men of his household;
— and when Avraham was circumcised, etc.,
— who was circumcised with him, etc.;"

p: — out of the sons of Heth.

— and so it is written of her,

,, — "I will rise before the Shechinah that is coming."

— for the middah of fear and dread

h: The name as the root of life

p: — And this is why there is mentioned here
— for it is written in the name of the Arizal
— is the root of the person's vitality,
— when one calls a man by his name
בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (קלא עַמּוּד א)
— in the holy Zohar on this parashah (131a)
— concerning the Resurrection of the Dead:
— "And the Holy One, blessed be He, will bring them down
— and call them by their names,"
— "and whatever the man would call it,
— for the world was created in the Holy Tongue,
— is the essence of its vitality.
— And so with the sons of Heth:
— "and You give life to them all"
— it shows that they drew out of them
— the entire root of their life
— And this is what is written,
— it alludes to the Ten Commandments.
— ten for the Giving of the Torah,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג יא עַמּוּד ב)
— And when it mentions their name
— it shows that they drew out of them

paragraphs.text: The Arizal, that a person's name is the root of his vitality, and so a sleeper wakes when called by name. Rav Tzadok names no work. The same teaching appears in Noam Elimelech, Shemos: “The name by which a person is called, such as Reuven or Shimon, is the name of the soul and not of the body. The proof is that when a person is asleep and we wish to wake him, if we push his body without calling him by name it is harder to wake him than if we call him by his name; for when a person sleeps his soul ascends and leaves his body.”

paragraphs.text: Parallels beyond the library: Be'er Mayim Chaim, Bereishis 23:16 (Chassidus) — Avraham would not bury Sarah while the field was still Ephron's, for holiness cannot rest under his domain. "For as long as Ephron's ownership is on the field, the holiness of God cannot rest in it so fully in any way."
